correctness.rationale: The Fock tensor reduction is exact because unitary coordinate rotation aligns any displacement with one coordinate. Gaussian double integration gives an exact positive HS cross trace. The Weyl generator commutator is a bounded compact Jacobi operator with coefficient |a|(1-r)sqrt(n+1)r^n; a uniform unitary conjugation integral yields an asymptotically sharp upper norm bound, while normalized coherent vectors at radius [2(1-r)]^(-1/2) yield the matching lower norm bound. The stable-rank constant and dimension transition follow by algebra. Finite standalone checks passed and are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Displacement and thermal/Fock radial contraction are canonical, independently motivated operations. Their commutator vanishes in operator norm but retains or increases Hilbert–Schmidt energy, with the precise dimension transition and displacement-independent stable-rank divergence rate e/2^(d+1). This jointly quantifies noncommutation and effective spectral spread in coherent-state smoothing. The invariant is natural rather than a chosen finite slice; its exact constant is needed to distinguish dimension-dependent smoothing regimes. It does not depend on speculative downstream applications.
